  <section v="12">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the revelation of the supernal treasure in the attribute of Netzach requires that the revelation be clothed in that attribute, achieved through the service of Netzach, and clarifies that Netzach does not awaken the treasure itself but rather the revelation occurs within it.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">10)</t>
    <t s="1">And 4)</t>
    <t s="2">And based on this, we can also explain what is said in the maamar, that the revelation and drawing down of the supernal treasure is in the attribute of Netzach,</t>
    <t s="3">so that the revelation of the supernal treasure will affect the attribute of Netzach within man,</t>
    <t s="4">so that it will have the power to overcome the opponents,</t>
    <t s="5">this is through the revelation and drawing down of the treasure being</t>
    <t s="6">(in the manner of enclothing)</t>
    <t s="7">in the attribute of Netzach.</t>
    <t s="8">And according to what was explained above regarding the matter of "And You are holy, enthroned upon the praises of Israel,"</t>
    <t s="9">that for the drawing down to be in a manner analogous to enclothing</t>
    <t s="10">("enthroned" from the term "sustenance")</t>
    <t s="11">in particular matters,</t>
    <t s="12">it is through service that is related to that particular matter in which the drawing down occurs</t>
    <t s="13">[although regarding the drawing down itself</t>
    <t s="14">(the drawing down of Atzmus)</t>
    <t s="15">it cannot be said that it is drawn down through service that is analogous to it],</t>
    <t s="16">it can be said,</t>
    <t s="17">that the same applies to the matter of the revelation and drawing down of the supernal treasure,</t>
    <t s="18">that for the revelation and drawing down to be in the attribute of Netzach within man, in a way that the revelation affects it,</t>
    <t s="19">it is through the service of Netzach.</t>
    <t s="20">And it can be said,</t>
    <t s="21">that this is what is said in the maamar "In the attribute of Netzach one can reach the supernal treasure, meaning that the revelation and drawing down of the supernal treasure is in the attribute of Netzach,"</t>
    <t s="22">that the intention of "meaning etc." is,</t>
    <t s="23">that this that Netzach reaches the supernal treasure is not that Netzach reaches the treasure in a way that it arouses the drawing down and revelation of the treasure</t>
    <t s="24">[similar to an arousal from below that arouses an arousal from above],</t>
    <t s="25">for in the aspect of the treasure, an arousal from below does not reach there</t>
    <t s="26">[and even service that comes from the essence of the soul, which reaches the innerness of Ein Sof, is only in a manner of elevation,</t>
    <t s="27">and the drawing down is only that a revelation is drawn from the aspect of the innerness, but not the innerness itself],</t>
    <t s="28">therefore it explains that this that Netzach reaches the supernal treasure is</t>
    <t s="29">(not that it arouses the revelation and drawing down itself,</t>
    <t s="30">but rather)</t>
    <t s="31">that the revelation and drawing down will be in the attribute of Netzach.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="13">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the reason for opening the treasures during war is for the sake of victory itself, which touches the essence of the soul, unlike conquest for territorial expansion, and the king therefore spends all his treasures without limit.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">10)</t>
    <t s="1">A)</t>
    <t s="2">And the maamar continues,</t>
    <t s="3">that the reason for opening the treasures at the time of war is,</t>
    <t s="4">because the main point of war is victory.</t>
    <t s="5">And this will be understood based on what the Mitteler Rebbe explains at length</t>
    <t s="6">regarding the greatness of the superiority and preciousness of the treasures</t>
    <t s="7">(and that nevertheless,</t>
    <t s="8">in order to win a war, the king spends all the treasures),</t>
    <t s="9">that even when sometimes the king wishes to show a great minister, his beloved and friend who is like his own soul, a precious vessel and the like that are in his possession,</t>
    <t s="10">he will not take from the treasures that have been hidden for many hundreds of years.</t>
    <t s="11">And only on very rare occasions,</t>
    <t s="12">when he makes a feast and celebration on the day of his wedding or the wedding of his son and the like,</t>
    <t s="13">then he will command to also bring out the precious vessels that have been hidden for a long time,</t>
    <t s="14">to show the preciousness of the glory of his greatness and the wealth of his royal honor.</t>
    <t s="15">But even then,</t>
    <t s="16">he does not show all the precious vessels that are in the treasures, only a part of them</t>
    <t s="17">(that are not so hidden),</t>
    <t s="18">and even from these vessels he only shows them to those sitting at the feast</t>
    <t s="19">(and does not give them away).</t>
    <t s="20">However, in order to win a war,</t>
    <t s="21">he brings out</t>
    <t s="22">(sells)</t>
    <t s="23">all the precious vessels etc. for the expenses of the war,</t>
    <t s="24">and there is no limitation in this,</t>
    <t s="25">for if the capital of his own treasury is insufficient, he will also take from the treasures that his fathers and forefathers stored up.</t>
    <t s="26">And it is explained there,</t>
    <t s="27">that this that in order to win the war he spends all his treasures,</t>
    <t s="28">is not because he wants to expand the border of his land by conquering another country or to increase his wealth through the spoils</t>
    <t s="29">[for then he would calculate how much capital is worthwhile to invest for this,</t>
    <t s="30">and he would not spend all his treasures,</t>
    <t s="31">and certainly would not waste them],</t>
    <t s="32">but rather in order to defeat the one who fights against him and opposes him.</t>
    <t s="33">For victory, to overcome the opponent, touches the innerness of the soul,</t>
    <t s="34">as is explained there at length.</t>
    <t s="35">And it can be said,</t>
    <t s="36">that what is said in the maamar, that the reason for opening the treasures at the time of war is because the main point of war is victory,</t>
    <t s="37">the intention in this is,</t>
    <t s="38">that the opening of the treasures at the time of war is not for the matter of conquest, that he will conquer another country and expand the border of his land,</t>
    <t s="39">but rather for the sake of victory,</t>
    <t s="40">that this</t>
    <t s="41">(victory)</t>
    <t s="42">is the main point of war.</t>
    <t s="43">And the same applies in the analogy,</t>
    <t s="44">that this that they give to Israel</t>
    <t s="45">(and in a manner of waste)</t>
    <t s="46">the supernal treasure in order to win the war is not in order to conquer the world and make it a dwelling place for Him, blessed be He,</t>
    <t s="47">through which the intention that the Holy One, blessed be He, desired to have a dwelling place in the lower worlds will be completed,</t>
    <t s="48">but rather,</t>
    <t s="49">for the sake of victory,</t>
    <t s="50">to overcome the opponent.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="14">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the three parts of the verse "Teach me the path of life" correspond to three types of service—Torah study, making the world a dwelling place, and victory over the opponent—with the latter being the most beloved, for which all treasures are given wastefully.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">10)</t>
    <t s="1">B)</t>
    <t s="2">And through this will be understood what the maamar brings,</t>
    <t s="3">that it is stated in Midrash Tehillim on the verse</t>
    <t s="4">"Teach me the path of life etc.,"</t>
    <t s="5">Dovid said before the Holy One, blessed be He: "Teach me the path of life etc.,"</t>
    <t s="6">the Holy One, blessed be He, said to Dovid: "You seek life? Look to the Torah etc."</t>
    <t s="7">And in Midrash Rabbah</t>
    <t s="8">it is stated,</t>
    <t s="9">"Fullness of joys is before Your face"</t>
    <t s="10">(do not read 'fullness' but 'seven')</t>
    <t s="11">these are the seven companies of tzaddikim that are destined to receive</t>
    <t s="12">the face of the Shechinah etc.,</t>
    <t s="13">"Who will tell us which company is the most beloved and pleasant among them etc."</t>
    <t s="14">(These)</t>
    <t s="15">that are destined to stand at the right hand of the Holy One, blessed be He,</t>
    <t s="16">as the verse says</t>
    <t s="17">"Pleasantness is in Your right hand forever."</t>
    <t s="18">And explanation is needed,</t>
    <t s="19">for at first glance,</t>
    <t s="20">the proof of the connection of Netzach to Israel is from the end of the verse "Pleasantness is in Your right hand forever,"</t>
    <t s="21">for according to the interpretation of the Midrash this refers to Israel,</t>
    <t s="22">so why does the maamar also bring the interpretation of the Midrash on the verse "Teach me the path of life, fullness of joys is before Your face."</t>
    <t s="23">And based on the above, we can say the explanation of this,</t>
    <t s="24">that the three matters in the verse</t>
    <t s="25">("Teach me the path of life,"</t>
    <t s="26">"Fullness of joys is before Your face,"</t>
    <t s="27">"Pleasantness is in Your right hand forever")</t>
    <t s="28">are three matters in the service of Israel,</t>
    <t s="29">through which the supernal treasures are revealed.</t>
    <t s="30">And "Teach me the path of life" is the matter of engaging in Torah</t>
    <t s="31">("You seek life? Look to the Torah"),</t>
    <t s="32">which is analogous to the giving of the Torah</t>
    <t s="33">(just as there, with awe and fear etc., so too here etc.),</t>
    <t s="34">that at the time of the giving of the Torah,</t>
    <t s="35">"the day of His wedding, this is the giving of the Torah,"</t>
    <t s="36">revelations were made from the supernal treasures,</t>
    <t s="37">similar to a mortal king who on his wedding day reveals from his treasures.</t>
    <t s="38">"Fullness of joys" these are the seven companies of tzaddikim etc., this is the service of Israel to make the world a dwelling place for Him, blessed be He.</t>
    <t s="39">For this is seven companies of tzaddikim</t>
    <t s="40">(specifically seven),</t>
    <t s="41">because since all matters of the world are in the number seven,</t>
    <t s="42">therefore also the service of the tzaddikim</t>
    <t s="43">(and "Your people are all tzaddikim")</t>
    <t s="44">to make the world a dwelling place for Him, blessed be He, is divided into seven,</t>
    <t s="45">seven companies of tzaddikim.</t>
    <t s="46">And it can be said,</t>
    <t s="47">that this is also what the Tzemach Tzedek, in his notes on Tehillim on the verse,</t>
    <t s="48">brings from our Sages, may their memory be blessed, this</t>
    <t s="49">(that "fullness of joys" is seven companies of tzaddikim)</t>
    <t s="50">in continuation of the exposition of our Sages, may their memory be blessed,</t>
    <t s="51">that "fullness of joys" are the seven strings that were in the harp of the Holy Temple,</t>
    <t s="52">for the intention is that the world is for Israel to make it a Sanctuary for Him, blessed be He</t>
    <t s="53">(as is also understood from the continuation of the explanation in the interpretation of the verse "And they shall make Me a Sanctuary"),</t>
    <t s="54">and the seven strings of the harp in the Holy Temple are the perfection of the seven matters of the entire world.</t>
    <t s="55">And this is that the matter of the seven companies of tzaddikim comes in continuation of the matter of the seven strings of the harp of the Holy Temple,</t>
    <t s="56">because the service of the seven companies of tzaddikim is to make the world a Sanctuary for Him, blessed be He.</t>
    <t s="57">And this matter</t>
    <t s="58">(that the world becomes a Sanctuary and dwelling place for Him, blessed be He)</t>
    <t s="59">is analogous to war in order to expand the border of his land,</t>
    <t s="60">for which he also takes from his treasures,</t>
    <t s="61">but not in a manner of waste.</t>
    <t s="62">"Pleasantness is in Your right hand forever" is the matter of the victory of Israel, that they overcome the opponent,</t>
    <t s="63">for this service is the most beloved and pleasant</t>
    <t s="64">("pleasantness")</t>
    <t s="65">of all the seven services,</t>
    <t s="66">for which they give all the treasures,</t>
    <t s="67">and in a manner of waste</t>
    <t s="68">(beyond calculation).</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
